clue.text: Girl seen on circle line?

parts.note: a lass is a girl, a word used mainly in northern England and Scotland
a circle is round in shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl spotted travelling on London's Circle line of the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle line' looks like the London Underground route, but 'circle' gives O and 'line?' alone defines; the question mark admits that a rope with a noose is only loosely a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed rope is a kind of line, cord thrown to catch cattle.

clue.text: Fruit making a very quiet appearance in o level experiment

indicators.note: an experiment tries things in new ways, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A fruit turns up unexpectedly in a school science exam practical.
explanation.walkthrough: O level was the British school exam at about 16; here 'experiment' rearranges A, PP, O and LEVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Love apple is an old name for the tomato, which is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: At first she sounds more annoyed — it's the drink!

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of she
sounds means the word is said aloud and spelt as heard

parts.note: more annoyed means angrier

explanation.surface: First she gets angrier, and the drink is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent ANGRIER is said like the end of the Spanish wine punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit, a refreshing beverage.

clue.text: Rhymes with "oldness", oddly

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh, of oldness

explanation.surface: Verses that chime with the word oldness, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems are verses, and rhymes is a loose word for poems.

clue.text: Prolonged studies — an arrangement is made

indicators.note: an arrangement made of the letters means the words studies and an are reordered

explanation.surface: Lengthy studies end with some arrangement being agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'an' of 'an arrangement' does double duty in the surface only; the fodder is STUDIES plus AN, and 'arrangement is made' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept going for a long time without a break is drawn out or continuous.

clue.text: Unprofessional dealings from keen doctors?

parts.note: keen means sharp, as of a blade
a group of doctors working together form a medical practice

explanation.surface: Clever medics accused of underhand behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits 'doctors' defines a practice by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest but not quite illegal business conduct is trickery, cheating within the rules.

clue.text: Eagerly expecting a good turn to turn up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Excitedly awaiting a kind deed to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good turn' reads as a kind deed, but it is three pieces; only 'turn' is flipped by 'to turn up', giving OG at the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agog is keyed up with excitement and anticipation.

clue.text: A madman, curiously, can't sue

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters of can't and sue are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A lunatic, strangely, is barred from taking legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is slang for a crazy person, an eccentric lunatic.

clue.text: Avoid 5 perhaps

definitions.meaning: to avoid something is to evade it
the answer at 5-down is underhand dealing, and a trick or scam is an example

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the answer at five, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to sidestep, and a crafty scheme or wangle is a dishonest ploy.

clue.text: Chap who has French wine dispatched to listener

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine

indicators.note: to a listener the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: dispatched means sent off

explanation.surface: A man who has French wine posted out to a radio listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent is a man's given name, so it names a chap.

clue.text: Trade warned off by one in uniform

parts.note: traffic means trade, often illicit dealing

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters of warned are rearranged

explanation.surface: A uniformed official warned against doing business.
explanation.walkthrough: A British traffic warden is a uniformed official who issues parking tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking enforcement officer in Britain wears a uniform, so is one in uniform.

clue.text: Took on new dept. Following trouble

indicators.note: following tells us the new arrangement comes after the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: new signals the abbreviation dept. is made over into a fresh order

parts.note: dept. is the usual abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: Someone took charge of a newly formed department after a spell of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the abbreviation to PTED; 'Following' places it after the word for fuss, not before.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or child is to take it on as one's own.

clue.text: Dismissive of first class rail

parts.note: A1 (read as AI) means first-class, the top rating in Lloyd's Register of shipping
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A traveller looks down on first-class rail travel.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the figure one, which crosswords read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy wave of the hand is offhand and casual, brushing something aside.

clue.text: Goes on about fish starting to swarm

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word swarm is taken

explanation.surface: Someone moans endlessly about fish beginning to crowd together.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain or nag persistently, so it is going on about something.

clue.text: Patient in lawsuit

explanation.surface: A sick person caught up in a court action.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's patient is called a case, and a lawsuit is a legal case heard in court.

clue.text: Drops in exchange rates

indicators.note: in exchange suggests swapping the letters of rates around

explanation.surface: A fall in currency exchange rates.
explanation.definitionFit: Teardrops are drops of salty liquid from the eyes.

clue.text: Looks to the audience for seaside entertainment venues

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners, a word said aloud

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, so looks means peers

explanation.surface: A performer looks out to the crowd at a seaside show.
explanation.definitionFit: British seaside piers are long jetties often holding theatres and amusements.

clue.text: Stalled, to delay permit of revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over completely, so the letters of delay, permit and of are rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is told to delay a permit while officials hold things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the fodder is DELAY PERMIT OF, rearranged as 'revolutionary' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer or negotiator who stalls is deliberately using delaying tactics to hold out.

clue.text: Actor seen with a little musician

parts.note: a bit is a little amount
a player is someone who plays an instrument

explanation.surface: A performer seen with a minor musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor performer with small roles is an actor in a tiny part.

clue.text: Energy required to steer a course?

parts.note: to direct is to steer or guide
a current is a course or flow, as of water in a channel

explanation.surface: A sailor needs determination to keep a ship on its route.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of 'course' as a flowing current; DC is electrical power flowing one way.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity flowing in one direction is a form of power supply, energy for circuits.

clue.text: Manage to rescind notice

indicators.note: to manage letters is to handle and arrange them, so rescind is rearranged

explanation.surface: Succeeding in cancelling a formal notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage to' looks like 'succeed in'; 'Manage' signals the anagram and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or spot something.

clue.text: Look closely and listen as I dance

indicators.note: listen as means take the word as it is heard

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like eye
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Watch carefully and hear me while I dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard, scrutinising.

clue.text: Actors' fling

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play taken together, the company, so the possessive reads as a plural noun

explanation.surface: Performers enjoy a brief romantic fling.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's performers together are its company, and to throw something is to toss it.

clue.text: Yields achieved from novice designer

indicators.note: achieved from says the letters are got from within the words novice designer

explanation.surface: Profits made by an inexperienced designer.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield ground is to give it up, surrender it.

clue.text: Key found in murderer's shed

indicators.note: found in means the key letter sits inside the murderer's name

parts.note: Cain, in the Bible, killed his brother Abel
B is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A vital key is discovered hidden in a killer's garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple hut or small wooden shelter is a basic building like a shed.

clue.text: Friend accepted sweetheart's ring

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A friend agreed to take a lover's engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it is the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal of bells is a ring, the full sound of bells rung together.

clue.text: Country post in which student is promoted

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, so in a down answer the letter rises higher

parts.note: mail means post
L stands for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A country posting where a student wins promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: L moves up within MAIL to give the West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African nation.

clue.text: Sun gets a leading role

explanation.surface: The sun lands a starring part.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Sun is a fixed celestial body of glowing gas, and a principal performer is the headline lead.

clue.text: Traditionalist who's tough on sources of debt, interest and expenditure

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another is written after it
the sources of words are their opening letters, taken from debt, interest and expenditure

parts.note: hard means tough

explanation.surface: A stubborn conservative takes a firm line on borrowing, interest rates and spending.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard clings stubbornly to old ways, opposing reform like a staunch conservative.

clue.text: Try and use a new form of English

indicators.note: new signals the letters of try, use and a are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Have a go at using a new style of English.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is an accent of the south-east of England spreading out from London along the Thames.

clue.text: Consciousness that one is trapped in time

indicators.note: trapped in means one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: a prisoner's time is a sentence served
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Awareness that a person is stuck in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' looks like the clock, but it is time served in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to feel and perceive is awareness, the state of being conscious.

clue.text: Game the French run for good measure

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union
le is French for the
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A game the French run as an extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for good measure' looks like a phrase meaning 'as an extra'; 'for good' is a link and 'measure' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edged strip for measuring length is a measuring tool.
